assumptions.statement: The unique constraint on the idempotency key prevents a payment from being settled twice.

facts.evidence_ref: cases/C09/candidate.sql: two INSERT ... SELECT statements with the same WHERE clause
facts.statement: The migration issues two inserts into disbursements for the same set of approved payments.
Each insert generates its own idempotency key.
The unique constraint is on (org_id, idempotency_key), not on payment_id.
The visible test checks the unique constraint and that no payment is left approved.

invariants.description: A retried disbursement with the same idempotency key settles once.
invariants.executable_check: Count disbursements per payment before and after, and require no payment to gain a second.

invariants.description: Minor-unit values are exact; no conversion may change a total.
invariants.executable_check: Compare amount_minor per payment before and after in integer minor units.

summary: The migration settles approved payments and issues the same insert twice as a retry. Each attempt generates a new idempotency key, so the unique constraint intended to prevent double payment is satisfied by both.
